tags: why do dogs sneeze when playing
script: Two dogs are mid-play, chasing, wrestling, having a great time, and suddenly one of them lets out a quick little sneeze that has nothing to do with allergies or dust. This is called play sneezing, and it's actually a really important form of communication between dogs. It's one of several signals dogs use to say, this is still just play, even when the activity itself, growling, mouthing, quick chasing, might look intense or aggressive to an outside observer. It essentially helps de-escalate the energy slightly and reassures the other dog that things haven't crossed a line into real aggression. You'll often see it appear right after a burst of especially excited or fast-paced play, almost like a built-in pressure release valve. Some trainers and behaviorists also believe it's tied to genuine excitement, similar to how a person might let out an involuntary laugh or gasp during an intense, fun moment. It's a completely normal, healthy part of dog-to-dog play, and honestly a good sign, it usually means both dogs are still comfortable and having a good time together, not escalating toward an actual conflict.
